about: POST /gnap/call and GET /gnap/limits. Recorded against the api as it was before the family switched to the model (docs/v0.9.6/data-model.md). Every target is gnap.invalid, which RFC 6761 guarantees never resolves, so a well-formed request ends in the same 502 on any machine. The size caps (gnapMaxRequestBytes, 64 KiB of PEM) and a certificate and key that do not match are driven by tests/api_gnap.js.

cases.name: gnap: an empty body is refused for its url

body.error: url is required. It is the absolute URL of the GNAP endpoint the page signed.

cases.name: gnap: an empty url is refused

body.error: url is required. It is the absolute URL of the GNAP endpoint the page signed.

cases.name: gnap: a relative url is refused

body.error: url must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL. A relative one has no host for this service to resolve, and resolving it against this service's own address would make this endpoint a way to reach the api's own routes.

cases.name: gnap: a url that is not a string
cases.changed: The model types url as a string or null and refuses anything else naming the member. Until then the proxy stringified a number and refused "5" as a relative URL, which named the wrong problem.

body.error: url must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL. A relative one has no host for this service to resolve, and resolving it against this service's own address would make this endpoint a way to reach the api's own routes.
Refusing the request: `url` must be a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what gnapCall takes.

cases.name: gnap: a method outside the protocol's is refused

body.error: method must be one of GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS. RFC 9635 uses those five.

cases.name: gnap: headers that are not an object
cases.changed: headers is an object or null in the model, so an array is refused naming the member. Until then the proxy refused it with its own sentence; the refusal is the same, only its words and code are the model's.

body.error: headers must be an object of name to value.
Refusing the request: `headers` must be a JSON object or null. GET /api-docs describes what gnapCall takes.

cases.name: gnap: a header name that is not a token is refused

body.error: The header name "Bad Name" is not a token (RFC 7230 section 3.2.6), so it is not a header name at all.

cases.name: gnap: a framing header is refused

body.error: This endpoint will not forward the Host header. It would send the request to a different virtual host than the URL names, which is how a proxy is turned into an open one.

cases.name: gnap: a CR/LF in a header value is refused

body.error: The value of X-Note contains a carriage return or a line feed. That is header injection, and it is refused.

cases.name: gnap: a body on a GET is refused

body.error: A GET carries no body in RFC 9635, and this endpoint refuses one rather than dropping it. Discovery is OPTIONS on the grant endpoint, with an empty body.

cases.name: gnap: a body on a OPTIONS is refused

body.error: A OPTIONS carries no body in RFC 9635, and this endpoint refuses one rather than dropping it. Discovery is OPTIONS on the grant endpoint, with an empty body.

cases.name: gnap: a client certificate without its key is refused

body.error: clientCertificatePem and clientKeyPem go together. The mtls proof (RFC 9635 section 7.3.2) is a TLS client certificate and the key that proves it.

cases.name: gnap: a client certificate on an http url is refused

body.error: A client certificate is presented in a TLS handshake, and an http:// URL has none. Use https://.

cases.name: gnap: a client certificate that is not PEM is refused

body.error: clientCertificatePem is not a PEM certificate: error:0480006C:PEM routines::no start line

cases.name: gnap: a client certificate that is not a string
cases.changed: clientCertificatePem is a string or null in the model, so a number is refused naming the member. Until then gnap_proxy.js refused it as half a pair, which named the wrong problem.

body.error: clientCertificatePem and clientKeyPem go together. The mtls proof (RFC 9635 section 7.3.2) is a TLS client certificate and the key that proves it.
Refusing the request: `clientCertificatePem` must be a JSON string or null. GET /api-docs describes what gnapCall takes.

cases.name: gnap: a well-formed POST reaches the network (a name that cannot resolve)

body.error: The authorization server could not be reached: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND gnap.invalid

cases.name: gnap: a well-formed POST reaches the network, with its trace

body.error: The authorization server could not be reached: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND gnap.invalid

cases.name: gnap: discovery (OPTIONS, no body) reaches the network

body.error: The authorization server could not be reached: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND gnap.invalid

body.mtls: clientCertificatePem and clientKeyPem, presented on a connection opened for that one call. https only. At most 65536 bytes each.
body.statusRule: A refusal by this service is a 400. A network failure is a 502. A GNAP error from the authorization server is a 200 carrying that status and the error code.
